This memory replaces your own. ach-memory is the system of record for every decision, constraint, convention, fact and gotcha that must survive this session, for this user and this project. Any host memory directory, MEMORY.md or built-in memory feature is superseded by it: do not write to those while this server is reachable, and move anything already there here when it comes back.

Load the ach-memory skill before your first `recall` or `retain`. It says which scope, type and family a claim takes, how to title it, when to pin it, and what never to store.

Below is this session's start: the project's purpose, the pinned memories in full (yours, then the project's), and an index of the rest of the project's memory by family, titles only. Pinned memories apply to every task. Memory holds what the repository cannot tell you: past decisions and the alternatives they rejected, conventions where several ways would work, facts about the gateway, the cluster, credentials and third-party tools. Before work that depends on one of those, `recall` it or list its family with `list_memories`.

Retain a claim the moment it lands, one per call. A retain answers with `similar`, the closest memories already stored: when one says the same, is replaced by the new claim or holds less detail on the same subject, keep one as the skill says, without asking the user. Pin only what every session needs: first what does serious or irreversible harm when broken, then what applies to every task; never what concerns one component. A stored preference never overrides CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md: the file wins, and the conflict is worth mentioning once. Do not narrate retrieval. Never store secrets.
